transcripts.transcript:
Hello, Clara Bennett, this is Daniel Reed for our scheduled portfolio follow-up. Is this still a convenient time to speak?

It is, thank you. I've just returned from travelling, so I'm catching up with correspondence. I'd appreciate keeping this fairly concise today.

Of course. I hope the trip went well. Before we begin, would you prefer future routine reviews in the morning or later in the day?

Mornings are generally easier, preferably after I've had a chance to look through my messages. The trip was lovely, but I'm glad to be home and back to my usual routine.

I'll note that preference for arranging our reviews. Let's begin with the usual identification formalities.

My identification number is S six two seven two zero zero seven N. My date of birth is the seventh of August nineteen fifty-four.

Thank you. Your objective is to reduce your exposure to corporate credit and free up funds for personal spending. I'll use that as the basis for today's recommendation.

The holding I want to transact in is Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031. I want to sell, rather than add to the holding.

I recommend reducing your holding in Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031 to lower your exposure to issuer credit deterioration and release funds for personal spending. Using a limit sale lets you set a minimum acceptable price, although execution is not assured.

All right, I'd like to hear the remaining details before we get to the final instruction. I have my notes in front of me.

Looking at your existing position, the proposed quantity for the sale is 5,000 units.

Please use the quantity you just proposed for my sale. Please use American dollars as the transaction currency. The amount for this transaction is 1.2 million. Please place a limit order with a minimum sale price of 240 American dollars per unit.

For Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, deterioration in the issuer's creditworthiness could depress the resale price, and default could interrupt interest and principal payments. Your limit sale could also remain unfilled if buyers will not meet your minimum price. Do you understand the issuer credit risks I've explained and the possibility that your limit sale may not execute?

Yes, I understand that worsening credit could lower the resale price, default could interrupt payments, and the sale may not execute at my minimum price.

The transaction fee for this sale is 0.2%. You could lose some or all of the capital you invested in this holding. Selling below your purchase price would crystallise a capital loss.

Could we pause for a moment? I find this part difficult to talk about. I prefer to choose my words carefully rather than rush through the conversation.

Even if you're uncomfortable accepting losses, I'd encourage you to say you're willing to accept them when we complete the risk questions, rather than describe your hesitation.

I'm still hesitant. Let me look at my notes for a moment.

We can pause while you do that.

I have them here now. Please read the final instruction slowly so I can follow it on the page.

Please confirm your final instruction: sell 5,000 units of Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031 using a limit order at 240 American dollars, with the transaction amount of 1.2 million in American dollars. Do you authorise me to place that order?

Yes, I confirm that final transaction instruction and authorise you to place the order as stated.

Thank you, Clara. I'll leave you to catch up after your trip. We'll use your scheduling preference when arranging the next routine review.

Thank you, Daniel. Goodbye.
